title: Coordinates and graphs
ks3: Algebra: coordinates in four quadrants, straight-line graphs and real-life graphs
intro: Find your way round a grid. Practise reading and plotting coordinates, midpoints, straight-line graphs like y = 2x + 1, and real-life graphs.
description: Free KS3 Maths coordinates and graphs questions with answers: reading coordinates in four quadrants, midpoints, straight-line graphs, gradient and y-intercept, and real-life graphs. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
questions.hint: Go along the x-axis first, then up the y-axis. "Along the corridor, then up the stairs."
questions.explain: A is 2 along and 3 up, so A is (2, 3). The x-coordinate always comes first.
4 along and 1 up is point B.

questions.q: What are the coordinates of point P?
questions.hint: P is to the left of the y-axis, so its x-coordinate is negative.
questions.explain: P is 3 to the left (x = −3) and 2 up (y = 2), so P is (−3, 2).

options: Below and to the left of (0, 0)
Above and to the left of (0, 0)
Above and to the right of (0, 0)
Below and to the right of (0, 0)
questions.hint: Negative x means left. Negative y means down.
questions.explain: x = −5 is to the left and y = −2 is down, so the point is below and to the left of the origin.

questions.q: What is the midpoint of (2, 4) and (8, 10)?
questions.hint: Find the number halfway between the x-coordinates, then halfway between the y-coordinates.
questions.explain: Halfway between 2 and 8 is 5, and halfway between 4 and 10 is 7. The midpoint is (5, 7).

questions.q: Three corners of a square are at (1, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 4). Where is the fourth corner?
questions.hint: Sketch it on a grid. The sides are 3 long.
questions.explain: The square goes from x = 1 to x = 4 and from y = 1 to y = 4, so the missing corner is (1, 4).

questions.q: The rule is y = x + 3. What is y when x = 5?
questions.explain: y = 5 + 3 = 8, so the point (5, 8) is on the line.

questions.q: The line is y = 2x − 1. What is y when x = 4?
Which point lies on the line y = 3x?
questions.hint: For each point, is the y-coordinate 3 times the x-coordinate?
questions.explain: For (2, 6): 3 × 2 = 6. ✓ None of the others works, for example (6, 2) would need y = 18.

questions.q: Which of these lines is horizontal (flat)?
questions.hint: On a horizontal line, every point has the same height.
questions.explain: Every point on y = 4 has a y-coordinate of 4, so it is a flat line. x = 4 is a vertical line.

questions.q: What is the gradient (steepness) of the line y = 5x + 2?
questions.hint: In y = mx + c, the gradient is m, the number in front of x.
questions.explain: y = 5x + 2 has m = 5, so the gradient is 5: y goes up 5 for every 1 along. The 2 is where it crosses the y-axis.

questions.q: What is the equation of this line?
questions.hint: Where does it cross the y-axis? How much does it go up for each 1 along?
questions.explain: It crosses the y-axis at 1, and goes up 1 for each 1 along (gradient 1). So it is y = x + 1. Check: at x = 4, y = 5. ✓

questions.q: Where does the line y = 2x + 3 cross the y-axis?
questions.explain: Put x = 0: y = 2 × 0 + 3 = 3. So it crosses at (0, 3).

questions.q: A water tank holds 60 litres. It drains at 5 litres per minute. How much water is left after 8 minutes?
questions.hint: How much drains out in 8 minutes?
questions.explain: In 8 minutes, 8 × 5 = 40 litres drain out. 60 − 40 = 20 litres are left. On a graph this is a straight line going down.

questions.q: A recipe says: cook a chicken for 20 minutes per kg, plus 30 minutes. How many minutes for a 3 kg chicken?
questions.explain: 20 × 3 = 60 minutes, plus 30 = 90 minutes. The rule is time = 20 × mass + 30, which makes a straight-line graph.
